thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: sustained p99 latency spike on /v1/stream/generate. 5m window shows p99 > 3.5s (SLO p99=2.0s). Affected model: rdx-13b-quant. Hot host: gpu-node-uk-03. Paging oncall: @maria_oncall.

maria_oncall: acked. I'm on it — starting triage.

james_sre: any obvious increase in 5xx or just latency? also which downstream consumers?

maria_oncall: seeing increased streaming stalls and very long tail during generation (clients report partial streams and stalls). p95 ~0.65s, p99 ~3.8s right now. No broad 5xx spike, a few client-side timeouts.

kevin_infra: pulling kernel/DMI logs from gpu-node-uk-03, past 30m:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=4321, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 12346.123456] gpu0: Correctable ECC error count rising: 18 -> 63 in 10m
[ 12352.654321] thermal: GPU sensor exceeded threshold, throttling
[ 12353.000111] nv_peer_mem: device reset/recover, seen stall on TPC
```
Looks like correctable ECCs + thermal throttle events. Could be flaky accelerator.

maria_oncall: thanks @kevin_infra. That matches the timeline for increased tail latency. Can we shift traffic off that host? Is there spare capacity in pool-uk-warm?

kevin_infra: spare warm capacity in pool-uk-warm and cpu-fallback pool in eu-west1. Recommended: drain gpu-node-uk-03, reroute streaming sessions with warm fallback for in-flight.

james_sre: note: streaming code keeps KV cache pinned to GPU. If we evacuate without clearing cache, some in-flight sessions will see a stall while cache rebuilds on the fallback node. Suggest enabling prefix-cache bypass for the reroute so fallback nodes build fresh KV.

maria_oncall: executing mitigation plan now: 1) enable canary fallback route for streaming -> rdx-13b-cpu for 20% traffic, 2) drain gpu-node-uk-03, 3) reduce batch size for streaming to reduce pressure. Commands:
```bash
# create fallback route
redwoodctl routes create fallback-stream --from /v1/stream/generate --to-model rdx-13b-cpu --weight 20
# drain host
redwoodctl host drain gpu-node-uk-03 --grace 120
# adjust batching
redwoodctl model update rdx-13b-quant --stream-batch-size 1
```

maria_oncall: applied fallback route and started drain. Initial metrics within 2m: p95 unchanged 0.6s, p99 down to 2.7s for overall traffic, stall-rate dropped from 12% -> 5%.

ella_pm: which customers saw timeouts/errors? any enterprise customers impacted? need to notify CS if SLA windows hit.

support_ops: quick list from logs past 15m:
- acme-ads (10% of requests) saw multiple stream stalls but no 5xx, client retries triggered
- skybox-ux (0.8% of requests) saw 504s from client side after 7s timeout
- internal-eval (0.3% of requests) had partial responses
Estimated customer impact: ~3.2% of production requests experienced stalls or elevated latency beyond SLA threshold in past 10m.

maria_oncall: thanks @support_ops — that aligns. No contractual 5xx SLA breach yet, but p99 SLO is breached. I'll coordinate a customer comms draft if this persists.

kevin_infra: hardware note: GPU card on gpu-node-uk-03 shows rising correctable ECC counts and a thermal excursion. If counts continue to increase after drain, plan is to power-cycle PCI bus and reprovision. If still flakey, escalate RMA with vendor.

james_sre: small follow-up — KV-cache eviction during drain caused one observed 30s stall for a single long-lived stream (session id 0x9f3a). To reduce risk, we should: 1) set TTL for KV to 5m, 2) pre-warm fallback nodes for active sessions. I'll open a short runbook item.

maria_oncall: doing a quick runbook checklist in thread:
- [x] page oncall (this thread)
- [x] identify hot host (gpu-node-uk-03)
- [x] enable fallback route -> rdx-13b-cpu (20%)
- [x] drain host (in progress)
- [x] reduce batch size for stream (done)
- [ ] prewarm KV on fallback nodes (james to action)
- [ ] hardware remediation (kevin to action if issue persists)
- [ ] customer comms if SLO still breached in 30m

james_sre: I prewarmed a cache sync job to push top prefixes to pool-uk-warm. Command:
```bash
redwoodctl cache prewarm --prefix-file /tmp/top-active-prefixes.txt --target pool-uk-warm
```
Started; ETA ~90s.

maria_oncall: drain finished. gpu-node-uk-03 now marked MAINT. p99 for streaming now ~1.9s across service (within SLO). Stall-rate ~1.2%. Rolling back temporary batch size change to default.

kevin_infra: good to hear. I'll keep host offline and run PCI reset + memory diagnostics. If ECC errors persist on reboot, I'll schedule a vendor RMA.

ella_pm: thanks team. Please capture customer impact and timeline for post-incident notes. Any action items for product or platform?

maria_oncall: action items captured:
- infra: full diagnostic + potential RMA for gpu-node-uk-03 (@kevin_infra)
- sre: add a KV prewarm step to the emergency drain runbook (@james_sre)
- product: review streaming SLO thresholds vs fallback behavior and consider shorter auto-fallback window (@ella_pm)
- support: prep customer comms template if we need to notify enterprise customers (@support_ops)

support_ops: I'll draft comms and share a link to the template in #customer-ops.

incident-bot: Incident summary event created: INC-2026-9350012345. Current status: mitigated (host drained). Next: postmortem in 24-48h.

maria_oncall: handing off to night oncall @james_sre in 30m. Short summary: p99 breach caused by gpu-node-uk-03 ECC+thermal flake, drained and traffic routed to cpu-fallback, p99 restored. If latency regresses or ECC counts increase on other hosts, escalate to infra.

james_sre: ACK handoff. I'll monitor for one rotation and start the post-incident checklist.

maria_oncall: thanks all — closing live mitigation. Will attach logs and timeline to the incident ticket.

incident-bot: Paging cleared. All active pages for INC-2026-9350012345 resolved.
